thread:
Maya Chen: Ran a focused kernel/batching sweep this morning across A100/H100/L40S for the new fused-compact Flash variant + paged-KV patch. Posting highlights and raw snippets.

ci-bot: benchmark job 1782101111 started (docker:perf:latest).

Maya Chen: TL;DR: H100 looks best overall for throughput; L40S has surprising host-pinned spill at seq>=6144; A100 shows KV-cache write amplification when batch>=8 with our default batching heuristic.

Samir Patel: can you paste the exact commands and a quick table?

Maya Chen: command I used: `./bench/run.py --model gpt-j-6b --kernel fused_compact --kv paged-kv --devices a100,h100,l40s --seq-sweep 512,1024,2048,4096,6144,8192 --batch-sweep 1,2,4,8,12`

Maya Chen: brief table (tokens/s median over 10 runs):
```
device | seq | batch | tokens/s | spill? | notes
A100   | 2048| 4     | 7200     | no     | stable
A100   | 6144| 8     | 4200     | yes    | KV write amp ~1.8x
H100   | 6144| 8     | 9800     | no     | best latency
L40S   | 6144| 4     | 3800     | yes    | cudaMallocAsync fallback
L40S   | 8192| 2     | 2200     | yes    | host-pinned spill & memcpy stall
```

Oliver Brooks: "KV write amp" = more GPU->host traffic? any profiling?

Maya Chen: yes — traced with perfkit + nvtx. On A100 at batch 8 the paged-KV path did many small writes to device cache, but our eviction policy causes synchronous writes out to host backing store (paged layer). Write amplification measured as total bytes written / logical kv bytes ~= 1.7-2.0.

Maya Chen: snippet from nvprof timeline: `MemcpyAsync(dst=host, bytes=~24MB) -> kernel stalled 2.1ms -> memcpy completes -> next token compute` repeated per micro-batch.

Jun Park: did you try the adaptive micro-batching heuristic (windowed accumulate) vs fixed micro-batches?

Maya Chen: yep. Adaptive reduces number of memcpy bursts by coalescing small micro-batches but increases tail latency. For A100 it lowered write amplification to ~1.2x at cost of +8% p99. For H100 the adaptive mode had negligible downside and is recommended there.

Lina Gomez: any allocator differences? L40S flagged cudaMallocAsync fallback — is that the allocator or the kernel memory path?

Maya Chen: L40S driver + our pinned allocator combo caused the fallback. When we hit >device-alloc budget the runtime falls back to pinned host allocations which triggers host spill memcpy. We saw that allocator threshold at ~82% resident usage for L40S under our workload.

Samir Patel: numbers for p50/p95 on H100 vs A100?

Maya Chen: pasted a tiny extract: `H100 seq=4096 batch=8 p50=120ms p95=220ms`, `A100 seq=4096 batch=8 p50=210ms p95=450ms` (A100 p95 inflated when spill occurs).

Oliver Brooks: interesting — H100 kernel scheduling wins there. Any variant differences: fused_compact vs fused_sparse vs strided-flash?

Maya Chen: fused_compact gave best steady throughput for medium seq (1k-6k). Strided-flash improved memory locality for very long seq (>8k) on H100 but needed more scratch memory. fused_sparse reduced compute for sparse attention patterns but wasn't tested thoroughly here.

Jun Park: did you capture KV hit/miss rates for paged-KV?

Maya Chen: yes — under this sweep paged-KV hit-rate stayed ~92% at seq<=4096, dropped to ~80% at 6144-8192 due to increased working set churn and more frequent evictions. That correlates with write amplification spikes.

Lina Gomez: any obvious quick wins?

Maya Chen: immediate mitigations: 1) enable adaptive micro-batching by default on H100; 2) increase allocator soft-limit on L40S for reserved device pages (avoids cudaMallocAsync fallback); 3) tune paged-KV eviction to favor recently accessed KV shards (reduce write-back frequency).

Samir Patel: can you open tickets for those and link perf traces?

Maya Chen: created perf-rt-482 (adaptive micro-batching rollout) and perf-rt-483 (pager eviction tune). Uploading nvtx traces to the perf bucket now.

Oliver Brooks: thanks — will take perf-rt-482 and try a small canary on H100 cluster tomorrow. :rocket:

Samir Patel: great work, Maya. If we can avoid host spill on L40S that's a big win for cost.

Maya Chen: +1. I'll follow up with short reproducible script and the nvtx slices in the ticket.

Lina Gomez: also add a quick note in the console rollout docs about the allocator knob so infra doesn't flip it accidentally.

Maya Chen: done, added doc note in the ticket.
